name: Ugly Blue
lede: Ugly Blue is a dim, grey-leaning [[blue]] from the xkcd 2010 crowd-name survey, one of several judgmental names ordinary respondents volunteered rather than a modifier of another word.

sections.title: A judgment, not a description
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd survey let respondents type any name for a swatch, and a number of them reached for blunt opinions like this one instead of a hue word; who first used it beyond the survey is undocumented [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for the region reads "moderate blue" [1].

Its closest standing color in our library is [[peacock-blue|Peacock Blue]], about 3.6 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[denim|Denim]] and [[steel-blue|Steel Blue]] nearby in the same muted-blue family [1]. The hex is a screen value, carrying no judgment of its own [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Ugly Blue covers at least 2% of the canvas in 104 of our 23,781 paintings, and by position in each painting's lightness order it is found in 54, more common than 51% of the named colors we track, as photographed [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 4.0 times the archive's baseline rate for that decade, and most often plays an accent, the role in 43% of matched paintings [2].

The earliest match is 1400, in a work by the Master of Saint Veronica, 610 years before the name's own 2010 record, a resemblance of hue in an aged photograph and no judgment on the painting itself, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
